hook_text: A finger points straight at you from a poster. What does it want?
clip_script: It is 1914, and Lord Kitchener wants you. Hundreds of thousands answer: friends join together in Pals battalions, and boys lie about their age. Women hand white feathers to men out of uniform. By 1916 it is not enough, and Britain passes conscription for men aged 18 to 41. Posters stir guilt and hatred; newspapers and letters are censored. But some men say no. Conscientious objectors carry stretchers, work on farms, or go to prison for their beliefs.
visual_style: A whiteboard recruitment poster with a pointing finger, queues at a recruiting office, a white feather, and a prison door closing on an objector.
pacing: Builds from volunteering to conscription to refusal.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to master conscription and propaganda.
